isolation: one child process per provider, 1800s budget
name: sample-decoder-fixture

timing_protocol.batch_data: seeded; every provider sees the same sequence
timing_protocol.cpu_bound_fraction: CPU submission-and-blocking fraction: CPU-busy time / total wall time. Near 1.0 means the GPU was not the bottleneck -- submission cost, or blocking on an implicit synchronization such as allocator pressure. Not a dispatch-only measurement
timing_protocol.l2_policy: never flushed inside a step -- this measures a training step, whose state is as warm as the previous step left it
timing_protocol.loss_trajectory: fresh batch per step, so agreement is not trivially satisfied
timing_protocol.peak_memory: measured after the optimizer state exists
timing_protocol.provider_order: seeded random, recorded; identical settings for every provider
timing_protocol.step: loss = workload.loss(model, batch); loss.backward(); opt.step(); opt.zero_grad()
timing_protocol.weights: built by the workload from a fixed seed, identical across providers

verification_policy.loss_scalar_and_finite: every loss in the trajectory, and the settled steps on either side of the timed blocks, must be a finite scalar; NaN or Inf marks the provider failed. Losses inside the timed blocks are not read: that would force a synchronization per step and destroy the measurement
verification_policy.loss_trajectory: diagnostic only -- reported, not gated. A defensible threshold depends on dtype and horizon, so a workload declares one via `loss_delta_threshold` or the trajectory stays an observation behind the correctness and finiteness gates
verification_policy.model_correctness: a workload may declare a whole-model gate: one untimed canonical forward/backward/optimizer step against both the original eager model and the bound-pair path a candidate replaces, checked against a calibrated per-role noise envelope, plus its loss trajectory over the calibrated horizon. A failure is recorded failed_at='model_correctness' and is never timed
verification_policy.preflight: every patched kernel through bench.provider.verify_pair_provider on its declaration's correctness workloads; a provider that fails is not timed
